title: GIS Analyst II
description:
Connect to a career at City Utilities! CU has been connecting our community to the services they need for every day life since 1945. From electricity to power our lives, clean water to be healthy, natural gas to stay warm, internet to keep businesses connected, to transit services to get them where they need to go.

Pay Details:
Minimum: $1,415.81/ week
Midpoint: $1,769.76

Work Schedule:
Monday–Friday 8:00am–5:00pm

Job Description:
PURPOSE OF POSITION:

The purpose of this position is to manage the entire lifecycle of City Utilities’ Enterprise Geographic Information System (GIS) as a GIS expert. Will be responsible for maintenance, strategic design, development, data quality, and network integrity, as well as implementing data policies and procedures. This includes training and supporting Utility personnel on GIS data usage and its value extraction. Uses technical skills to fulfill internal and external customer requests and applications. These skills should include ArcGIS spatial analysis, Model Builder, Python, Arcade, or programming for data modeling, and Data Interoperability tools. Uses these tools for system data modeling, reporting, custom tracing, and visualizations. Uses communication and problem-solving skills to guide decisions on data integrity throughout the design, development, and deployment of mission-critical information for Utility operations. This ensures a scalable, secure, and efficient GIS infrastructure.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:

1.    An “expert” or highly experienced individual with utility institutional knowledge using the ArcGIS suite of products.
2.    Supports the Supervisor-GIS with leading, overseeing, and supervising other GIS personnel. Leads, trains, and delegates GIS staff under the direction of the Supervisor-GIS, with regards to GIS related projects.
3.    Manages ArcSDE version activity including:
a.    Deals with conflict versions and identifying/addressing version/design inconsistencies.
b.    Develops workflows for all processes that impact the ArcSDE database. This includes daily editing and data maintenance and ad hoc projects.
c.    Reviews ArcSDE log files on a regular basis and makes necessary adjustments if required.
d.    Reviews ArcSDE tables to confirm there are no orphaned states, orphaned records in delta tables, and that user log tables are being successfully truncated.
e.    Reviews logs and data base lineage to confirm successful execution of compress and analyze.
f.    Oversees the process of reconciling and posting all version activity.
4.    Responsible for providing technical leadership for GIS staff, as well as training Engineers/Designers, field mobile users (rugged device, tablet, and phone), and other users of GIS by providing large group, small group and one-on-one training.
5.    Technical Expert:
a.    Responsible for overseeing all facets of the ArcGIS suite of products, including ArcGIS Pro, ArcMap, ArcGIS Portal, ArcGIS Server, and ArcGIS Online (AGOL).
b.    Provides in-depth knowledge of utility network data management using ArcGIS Utility Network and Geometric Network.
c.    Accountable for Model Builder, Arcade, or Python script for geoprocessing automation.
d.    Uses Data Interoperability tools like Spatial FME or ETL/ELT frameworks.
e.    Provides support for enterprise GIS deployments and integrations.
6.    GIS Infrastructure Design and Management:
a.    Designs, implements, and maintains a scalable, secure, and performant GIS infrastructure using ArcGIS Pro, ArcMap, Portal, AGOL, and related systems.
b.    Integrates GIS with other enterprise systems (e.g., AIM, Mobile, GLK, WLK) to ensure data consistency.
c.    Manages user accounts, access controls, and permissions for the GIS System.
7.    Uses Model Builder or programming/scripting to create geoprocessing models that can automate data conversion, maintenance, and create reports or visualizations.
8.    Utility Network Data Management:
a.    Develops and implements data standards and best practices for utility network data within the ArcGIS Utility Network.
b.    Oversees the creation, validations, and maintenance of accurate and up-to-date utility network data layers.
9.    Product development and functionality:
a.    Analyzes user requirements from various utility departments and translates them into technical specifications for GIS functionalities specific to gas, water, electric, and fiber networks.
b.    Collaborates with developers, contractors, and fellow IT staff to create new features, applications, and tools for efficient utility network management using ArcGIS Pro and Utility Network tools.
c.    Stays up to date on emerging GIS technologies and trends relevant to the utility industry.
d.    Creates Esri based applications utilizing core business tools.
10.    System Administration and Security:
a.    Monitors system performance, troubleshoots technical issues, and performs system maintenance for ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Portal, ArcGIS Online (AGOL) and related software.
b.    Implements and maintains security measures to safeguard sensitive utility network data.
c.    Provides assistance with the installation, configuring, and maintenance of the ArcGIS Enterprise platforms.
11.    Responsible for maintaining the quality and integrity of all network data on a regular basis which includes but is not limited to connectivity, corrective actions, loops, multi-feeds, system integrations, as well as mission-critical updates such as electric feeder changes, emergency valve isolation analysis, boil advisory analysis, etc.
12.    Prepares and presents a variety of written and oral reports.
13.    Leads in the variety of planning, design, and analysis work in order to administer GIS activities.
14.    Implements the Supervisor-GIS vision with communicating requirements and priorities that affect the daily activities of employees in the GIS group.
15.    Develops and writes GIS training documentation for all enterprise GIS users. Documentation includes system architecture design, web services, tools, developing standards, quality control procedures, and workflows for GIS systems and related applications.
16.    Responsible for the development and management of project specifications and graphic standards of GIS data projects for consultants and internal project managers.
17.    Uses complex spatial and data analysis tools and techniques within ArcGIS (e.g. Spatial Analyst, 3D Analyst, Insights, Geoprocessing tools, etc.) utilizing GIS data, related add-ons, and relational databases to meet the needs of internal and external customer requests, including but not limited to modeling of system data, reporting, custom tracing, and specialized views.
18.    Applies the basics of Data Interoperability (Spatial FME and ETL/ELT) and how to apply this framework in an enterprise setting.
19.    Administers ArcGIS Enterprise deployment, upgrades, and application development (ArcGIS Server, ArcGIS Portal, ArcGIS Online, ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Desktop, etc.). This includes defining the customers’ requirements, establishing the data source(s), building the visualization (i.e., map display/document), publishing the data as a service, working with IT to establish an account, testing the application and training the user(s).
20.    Performs other project-related duties or functions as needed when critical to business function.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Education and Experience:

- A bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in geospatial sciences, geography, geology, planning, information technology, construction technology, or in a related field is required. Exceptional related experience may be considered in lieu of a college degree on a year-for-year basis.

- A minimum of five years of recent utility electric, natural gas, water or broadband experience in an engineering or operations supporting role is required.

- A strong background supporting GIS networks using Esri ArcGIS applications, with at least three-years of Esri ArcSDE experience, is required.

- Python, Arcade, or Model Builder experience is required.

- Spatial FME and/or Spatial ETL/ELT experience is preferred.

- Geocomputational skills preferred.

- Utility Network Data Management experience preferred.

Licensing/Certification:

Must have a valid driver’s license (minimum Class F).

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

- Proficient with:

- Current Esri products (ArcGIS Suite of products).

- Current ArcGIS Server or related Esri technologies including ArcGIS Desktop, ArcGIS Pro, publishing services, and deployments in virtual or physical environments.

- ArcSDE administration.

- Working knowledge of:

- Enterprise-scale utility GIS implementation.

- Integrating with other Utility T&D applications (i.e., System Modeling Software, Work Management, Customer Information System, Outage Management, etc.).

- Using Model Builder.

- GIS Development or scripting languages (i.e, Python, Arcade) for customizing ArcGIS functionalities.

- Data Interoperability, Spatial FME and ETL/ELT tools.

- Ability to:

- Architect, implement, and administer enterprise GIS solutions and systems that leverage ArcGIS Enterprise platforms: ArcGIS Desktop, ArcGIS Server, ArcGIS Portal, and ArcGIS Online.

- Delegate and effectively coordinate the activities of others.

- Quickly learn and become familiar with technical subjects.

- Communicate clearly, concisely, and convey technical information in non-technical terms.

- Work courteously with customers, co-workers, and individuals in other departments.

- Demonstrated abilities in meeting deadlines and scheduling of work for timely completion.

- Effectively utilize a range of digital tools and platforms, including but not limited to Microsoft Office Suite, enterprise software, artificial intelligence-enhanced applications, and self-service systems. Must possess a willingness and capacity to learn and adapt to emerging technologies, including mobile devices, cloud-based systems, and data-driven platforms relevant to utility operations.

- General understanding of ArcFM configuration and functionality.

- High analytical, organizational, problem-solving, and relational skills.

- Excellent oral and written presentation skills.

- Strong understanding of enterprise GIS deployments and associated integrations.

- Maintain adherence to all company policies.

Physical Requirements:

Typically, sedentary work.  Ability to express or exchange ideas by means of the spoken word and receive detailed information through oral communication.  Must be able to pass the Ishihara color vision test and/or be able to visually differentiate and identify colors on computer monitor. Substantial movements of the wrists, hands, and/or fingers, and close visual acuity to operate a computer is required. Bending and stooping may be required for filing and file retrieval.  Must be able to visually differentiate between color-coded lines and symbols associated with utilization of geospatial software.  May be required to lift up to 20 pounds occasionally.

Working Conditions:

Duties are primarily performed in an office environment.  Will require occasional late hours and weekend work to perform system maintenance while users are off the system. Optional hybrid work from home schedule after probationary period.

Miscellaneous Requirements:

- Employee must remain alert and aware of their surroundings at all times and maintain the ability to respond to changing circumstances in a timely manner.

- Must be able to work successfully with diverse groups of people.

TESTING
Testing may be required.

EEO

title: Sr. NERC or NERC Compliance Specialist
description:
Connect to a career at City Utilities! CU has been connecting our community to the services they need for every day life since 1945. From electricity to power our lives, clean water to be healthy, natural gas to stay warm, internet to keep businesses connected, to transit services to get them where they need to go.

Pay Details:
NERC Compliance Specialist:
Salary Grade 58
Minimum: $1,618.87/ weekly
Midpoint: $2,023.60

Sr. NERC Compliance Specialist:
Salary Grade 59
Minimum: $1,851.10/ weekly
Midpoint: $2,313.86

Work Schedule:
Monday - Friday, 8:00 am - 5:00 pm.

Job Description:
PURPOSE OF POSITION:
Under the close or general supervision of the Supervisor – Electric Reliability Compliance or designee, implements CU’s electric reliability compliance program and assesses compliance with all applicable North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) standards across CU. This position also supports compliance efforts to meet Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) requirements (information protection and Standards of Conduct) and Southwest Power Pool (SPP) governing documents.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:
1.    Develops, implements, and administers internal control processes and procedures designed to track compliance.
2.    Reviews compliance documentation and coordinates changes with CU subject matter experts as needed.
3.    Collaborates with CU and regulatory agency staff as needed to collect and prepare documentation for audits and data requests while meeting timelines for reporting.
4.    Performs gap analyses and mock audits to proactively determine compliance risk in systems, plans or procedures.
5.    Organizes and manages software applications to ensure essential tasks and documentation are completed to support compliance.
6.    Monitors NERC, FERC, and other industry media and regulatory agencies for ongoing standards development activity. Communicates this information to the appropriate areas.
7.    Provides training and technical guidance to subject matter experts on emerging reliability and security topics to promote continuous improvement and reduce risk of non-compliance.
8.    Investigates and documents events to assess compliance, perform risk analysis, identify root causes and corrective actions.
9.    Provides updates and progress reports regarding CU’s compliance status.
10.    Stays current on applicable regulatory requirements and advises CU staff of changes.
11.    Represents CU’s interests at committee and/or advisory group meetings.
12.    Assists in the administration of information protection program requirements.
13.    Performs other related duties as required or assigned by management.

QUALIFICATIONS:
Education and Experience:
Bachelor’s degree in engineering, mathematics, communications, information technology, computer science, business, or related discipline is required. A combination of higher education course(s) and exceptional work experience may be considered in lieu of a bachelor’s degree on a year-for-year basis.

NERC Compliance Specialist:
A minimum of three years’ recent experience in utility/energy industry or like business in a regulatory function, such as: auditing, cyber security, energy management systems (EMS, SCADA), compliance, or utility operations (generation, transmission, or distribution) is required.

Sr. NERC Compliance Specialist:
A minimum of five years’ recent experience in utility/energy or like business in a regulatory function, such as: auditing, cyber security, energy management systems (EMS, SCADA), compliance, or utility operations (generation, transmission, or distribution); of which, three years of recent progressively responsible experience in a NERC compliance role is required. Any listed advanced certification may be considered in lieu of one year’s required experience.

Licensing/Certification:
Must have a valid driver’s license (minimum Class F).

Sr. NERC Compliance Specialist:
Active advanced certification(s) such as Certified Compliance & Ethics Professional (CCEP), Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP), Certified Information System Auditor (CISA) or similar discipline is preferred.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:
**The Sr. NERC Compliance Specialist assumes greater responsibility and accountability for skills and abilities.

- Ability to:

- Self-start and motivate others as well as understand and communicate reliability standards and requirements and convey technical information in non-technical terms.

- Become familiar with various online platforms used for submitting information to NERC and the Regional Entity.

- Follow directions in a dynamic and sometimes stressful environment dealing with regulatory agencies.

- Assertively engage CU staff through evidence reviews to determine CU’s state of compliance to regulatory standards.

- Follow prioritized work tasks and adjust as necessary, based on changing requests.

- Interact with regulatory agencies in a professional manner.

- Coordinate and train with internal departments to meet deadlines.

- Monitor or actively observe industry stakeholder groups related to NERC compliance (e.g., compliance monitoring and enforcement, standards development process, SPP stakeholder groups, and the like).

- Effectively utilize a range of digital tools and platforms, including but not limited to Microsoft Office Suite, enterprise software, artificial intelligence-enhanced applications, and self-service systems. Must possess a willingness and capacity to learn and adapt to emerging technologies, including mobile devices, cloud-based systems, and data-driven platforms relevant to utility operations.

- Strong organizational skills to manage documents and meet schedules for reports and activities required by regulatory deadlines.

- Strong technical writing, computer, and group leadership skills.

- A basic understanding of NERC and FERC requirements.

- Public speaking/presentation skills.

- Good customer service skills to interact with other departments.

- Proficiency with various online platforms used for submitting information to NERC and the Regional Entity, including, but not limited to, Align and the secure evidence locker.

- Good communication and interpersonal skills.

- Maintain adherence to all company policies.

Physical Requirements:
Typically, sedentary work. Ability to express or exchange ideas by means of the spoken word and receive detailed information through oral communication. Substantial movements of the wrists, hands, and/or fingers, and close visual acuity to operate a computer. Also, may require lifting up to 20 pounds, on occasion.

Working Conditions:
Duties are normally performed in an office with some occasional field trips. Travel outside of Springfield, MO may be required occasionally. May be required to work non-standard hours, holidays, and schedules occasionally.

Miscellaneous Requirements:

- Employee must remain alert and aware of their surroundings at all times and maintain the ability to respond to changing circumstances in a timely manner.

- Must be able to work successfully with diverse groups of people.

TESTING
Testing may be required.

title: Manager or Supervisor – Electric Reliability Compliance
description:
Connect to a career at City Utilities! CU has been connecting our community to the services they need for every day life since 1945. From electricity to power our lives, clean water to be healthy, natural gas to stay warm, internet to keep businesses connected, to transit services to get them where they need to go.

Pay Details:
Supervisor – Electric Reliability Compliance:
Salary Grade 60
Minimum: $2,075.10/weekly
Midpoint: $2,645.75

Manager – Electric Reliability Compliance:
Salary Grade 61
Minimum: $2,372.76/weekly
Midpoint: $3,025.27

Work Schedule:
Monday - Friday, 8:00 am-5:00 pm.

Job Description:
PURPOSE OF POSITION:
Under the direction of the Senior Legal/Regulatory Counsel or designee, manages electric reliability compliance activities across all applicable areas of the Utility to adhere to reliability standards of the North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC), related requirements of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), and Southwest Power Pool (SPP) criteria.

Manager – Electric Reliability Compliance:
This role serves as the primary internal subject matter expert on NERC, Midwest Reliability Organization (MRO) and applicable Regional Entity reliability standards and coordinates compliance activities across operations, engineering, IT/cybersecurity, and all internal stakeholders.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:
Supervisor – Electric Reliability Compliance:
1.    Oversees the development, maintenance, and implementation of the Electric Reliability Compliance Program processes and metrics to support CU’s culture of compliance in accordance with reliability standards.
2.    Evaluates Utility operations for compliance with NERC standards and recommends policy level changes to enhance compliance with those requirements.
3.    Monitors NERC and related industry media for emerging compliance issues and communicates this information to the CU compliance committee and other appropriate areas.
4.    Assists CU departments and subject matter experts in developing and implementing compliance procedures to ensure compliance.
5.    Provides or arranges technical and regulatory staff training on reliability standards.
6.    Collects and reviews internal compliance documents and ensures an accurate compliance database is maintained for audits.
7.    Leads internal effort for coordination and preparation for reliability audits, surveys, and submission of compliance reports and documentation.
8.    Supervises compliance staff to ensure all deadlines are met and department goals are accomplished.
9.    Assists in the implementation of the FERC Standards of Conduct compliance program for wholesale market participation.
10.    Assists in the administration of information protection program requirements including Critical Energy Infrastructure Information (CEII) and related CU/SPP confidential/non-disclosure agreements.
11.    Performs other related duties as requested by management.

Manager – Electric Reliability Compliance:
**In addition to the Supervisor classification. The Manager classification is expected to perform these functions with increased proficiency, autonomy, and ownership.
1.    Serves as the Compliance Manager of CU’s Compliance Program.
2.    Leads the CU Electric Reliability Compliance Committee (ERCC).
3.    Coordinates CU participation in Small Group Advisory Sessions, technical conferences, and workshops on key issues.
4.    Reviews instances of potential noncompliance and makes final decisions or recommendations to Chief Compliance Officer or designee on appropriate disposition.
5.    Advises the Chief Compliance Officer and other senior leadership with regards to NERC/MRO audit findings, potential needs for self-reporting, penalty negotiations, development of mitigation plans, and tracking of mitigation plans to completion as needed.
6.    Represents the Utility on various regional, state, and federal reliability committees as appropriate, with emphasis on MRO and NERC committees, and promotes participation of NERC and other CU employees in such committees.
7.    Helps identify and propose related training needs, and assists in investigating and advising on employee questions and concerns regarding the FERC Standards of Conduct.
8.    Participates in and contributes to CU’s Operational Resiliency Committee, provides support as needed for GridEx planners and participants, and represents the compliance function in cross-functional planning discussions.
9.    Identifies process improvement opportunities based on planning exercises, incident investigations, root cause analysis, and industry best practice.
10.    Provide periodic status reports, metrics, and dashboards on compliance performance, open mitigation plans, and key risks to senior leadership, the governing board/commission, and relevant committees.
11.    Builds relationships with compliance counterparts at other municipal utilities in SPP and MRO by proactive participation in meetings, forums industry events, conferences, and personal outreach to encourage sharing of best practices, problem solving, and early awareness of emerging compliance issues.

QUALIFICATIONS:
Education and Experience:
Bachelor’s degree in applicable engineering, business, information technology or related discipline is required from an accredited college or university.

In lieu of a bachelor’s degree, an equivalent combination of education, and/or certifications, and progressively responsible experience in engineering, business, information technology, or related disciplines may be considered. Supervisor - minimum of two years of recent supervisory experience required. Manager - minimum of four years' recent supervisory experience is required.

Supervisor – Electric Reliability Compliance:
A minimum of five years related progressively responsible electric industry experience in relevant regulatory compliance, engineering, transmission, generation, information services or technology is required. Recent supervisory experience is preferred.

Manager – Electric Reliability Compliance:
A minimum of seven years related progressively responsible electric industry experience in relevant regulatory compliance, engineering, transmission, generation, information services or technology is required. A minimum of four years' recent supervisory experience is required.

Licensing/Certification:
Must have a valid driver’s license (minimum Class F).

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:
**The Manager classification assumes greater responsibility and accountability for skills and abilities.

- Advanced understanding of electric utility bulk power operations.

- Knowledge of NERC standards and ability to assess the Utility’s compliance with those requirements.

- Excellent organizational skills to independently manage documents and meet schedules for reports and activities required by regulatory deadlines.

- Proficiency with operating personal computers and use of Microsoft Office suite, including SharePoint.

- Excellent oral and written communication skills.

- Excellent interpersonal skills that will motivate others, while having the capacity to assertively engage others as needed to assess compliance.

- Ability to:

- Skillfully handle personnel problems and situations involving tact, discipline, and employee recognition.

- Make mature decisions without supervision while maintaining confidentiality regarding regulatory compliance issues.

- Plan, organize, and coordinate work with a high degree of accuracy and make mature decisions in managing risks.

- Be current with rapidly changing technological and regulatory advancements and provide direction as to their implementation.

- Effectively utilize a range of digital tools and platforms, including but not limited to Microsoft Office Suite, enterprise software, artificial intelligence-enhanced applications, and self-service systems. Must possess a willingness and capacity to learn and adapt to emerging technologies, including mobile devices, cloud-based systems, and data-driven platforms relevant to utility operations.

- Ensure EEO compliance according to CU’s policy 2.29 as well as all other company policies.

Physical Requirements:
Typically, sedentary work. Ability to express or exchange ideas by means of the spoken word and receive detailed information through oral communication. Substantial movements of the wrists, hands, and/or fingers, and close visual acuity to operate a computer is required.

Working Conditions:
Duties are normally performed in an office with some occasional field trips. Travel outside of Springfield, Missouri may be required occasionally. May be required to work non-standard hours, holidays, and schedules occasionally.
